> **Generated — do not hand-edit this table.** Each row's source is
> `_registry/<DEF###>.row.md` (one file per defect); rebuild with
> `scripts/registers/gen_registers.py gen def`. See [How to add a defect](#how-to-add-a-defect).

The processed record of every **defect** — a thing that is broken or wrong versus the
spec. Two sources feed it:

- **User-reported** — filed in-app (`POST /v1/feedback/bug` → `bug_reports` table on
  melehost), triaged by [`/fix-bugs`](../../.claude/commands/fix-bugs.md). The DB is the
  intake queue; **this file is the processed record.** When a report is worked, it gets a
  `DEF###` here.
- **Prompt-reported** — a defect Saiful (or Claude) spots in a session with no in-app
  report behind it. No `bug_reports` row; still gets a `DEF###` here when processed.

Sibling register for *planned* change (new work, not fixes): [`../forward_planning/cr_list.md`](../forward_planning/cr_list.md).
Governance rationale: decision **D-058** in [`../initial_specs/11_decisions/decision_log.md`](../initial_specs/11_decisions/decision_log.md).

## How to add a defect

**This table is generated** — never edit it by hand. A shared monolithic table gets
*swept*: on the shared `main` checkout the second committer captures the whole index and
silently steals another track's uncommitted rows (the 2026-07-24 DEF095/096 incident —
[CR081](../forward_planning/CR081_registers_are_architect_write_only/CR081_registers_are_architect_write_only.md)).
One file per item removes the shared write entirely. Instead:

1. **The Architect mints the ID.** Ask for the next `DEF###` (zero-padded, sequential,
   never reused) — one minter avoids the ID-collision race. Pre-triage items use a
   topic-slug handle until the ID is assigned.
2. **The item's domain owner writes one row file** — `_registry/DEF###.row.md` containing
   that defect's single markdown table row (columns below). One file per item is a disjoint
   write-path, so two tracks never collide. **Source** is `bug:<short-id>` (first 8 chars of
   the `bug_reports.id` UUID) for user-reported, or `prompt` for prompt-reported.
3. **Regenerate + pathspec-commit:** `python scripts/registers/gen_registers.py gen def`,
   then `git commit -m "…" -- docs/defect/_registry/DEF###.row.md docs/defect/def_list.md`.
   Never bare `git commit` / `-am` / `git add -A` (those re-introduce the sweep).
4. Fix it on a branch; the fix commit carries `fix(bug:<short-id>): <summary> (AT:R<N> DEF###)`
   (user-reported) or `fix(<scope>): <summary> (AT:R<N> DEF###)` (prompt-reported). Update
   your row file's **Fix** hash + **Status** and regenerate.
5. For a defect needing its own root-cause / design write-up, create
   `docs/defect/DEF###_<snake_case_topic>/` and link it from the row.

**Status** is one of exactly four tokens — `open` · `fixed` · `wontfix` · `dropped` —
and nothing else. **Enforced** (DEF203) by `gen_registers.py verify` and by
`backend/tests/unit/test_registers_no_drift.py`; the vocabulary itself lives in
`scripts/registers/gen_registers.py`.

Put qualifiers in the **description** column, never here. This legend used to read
`resolved · wont_fix · closed · open` and did not mention `fixed`, which was the second
most common value in the register — the drift it licensed cost real accuracy: 22 distinct
status values across 221 rows, four spellings of "fixed", and 20 cells holding whole
sentences. A cell holding prose is invisible to every filter that matches a token, always
in the same direction, so the backlog reads shorter than it is.

| DEF039 | 2026-07-09 | prompt | other | `reputation_events` has no DB partial-unique index on its `(user_id, event_type, ref_id)` dedup anchor — dedup is app-code-only (a SELECT-then-INSERT race), so concurrent same-ref awards can double-insert (defense-in-depth gap on a monetized currency). Fix: partial unique index (`WHERE ref_id IS NOT NULL`, since ref_id is nullable and award() only dedups when given one) on both the ORM model (`sqlite_where` too, for `create_all()`-backed tests) and migration 0015 for Postgres. `award()` now catches the resulting `IntegrityError` on the losing side of a race, rolls back, and returns 0 — same contract as the existing dedup-check hit. +1 regression test simulating the race (`test_reputation_service.py`). Migration verified via SQLAlchemy model load + the SQLite-parity test only — the Mac has no live Postgres to dry-run `alembic upgrade head` against (pre-existing repo constraint: the full chain already fails on SQLite at an earlier, unrelated Postgres-only migration); real verification happens at `/promote-to-alpha`. | fixed | — | AT:R54 |
| DEF040 | 2026-07-09 | prompt | other | Account merge mid-week re-keys `reputation_events` and sums lifetime `reputation` but does not recompute the adopter's current-week `league_members.points` — a mid-week claim can undercount current-week league standing (lifetime reputation stays correct). (CR004 audit round-1 finding F5) Root cause: the league-seat re-key (`_rekey_skipping_conflicts` on `LeagueMemberRow`, conflict_col=week) drops the orphan's seat outright whenever both sides already hold one for the current week — the common case — leaving the adopter's `points` frozen at its pre-merge value even though the orphan's `reputation_events` (re-keyed just above it) now belong to the adopter. Fix: after the reputation re-key, if the adopter holds a current-week seat, recompute its `points` as a full resync (`sum(reputation_events.points)` over the current ISO week's bounds via `league_service.week_end()`) rather than a delta — correct regardless of which side's seat survived. +1 regression test that fails at `3 == 11` without the fix. | fixed | — | AT:R54 |

| DEF049 | 2026-07-11 | prompt | other | Streak-milestone **credit double-grant under concurrency** (monetized currency). `reputation_service._grant_milestone` calls `award(…, always_record=True)` then grants credits (`user.credit_balance += credits` + `SubscriptionEventRow`) **unconditionally**, without checking whether *its* `award()` call actually wrote the guard row. After DEF039 added the partial-unique index + `IntegrityError`→rollback→return-0 to `award()`, the loser of a concurrent same-milestone race rolls its guard-row insert back yet **still grants credits** → a one-time double credit. Fix: opt-in `_raise_on_race` flag on `award()` — the milestone path passes it, so a race-loss raises instead of returning 0, and `_grant_milestone` skips the credit grant; all other callers keep the return-0 contract. +1 regression test. | DEF056 | 2026-07-13 | prompt | other | **Room's structured Verdict ignores the 12-agent debate; PM prose can contradict it** — found verifying a live RXT convene. `_assemble_verdict()` computed action/size/entry/stop/target from `base_price` + `mandate.risk_score` tier + structural-only `check_mandate_compliance()`, set before any agent speaks; none of the 12 agents' conclusions (incl. the Trader's own recommendation) ever reached it. On RXT, Trader/Conservative Debator/PM all independently concluded WAIT/REJECT using real data, yet the stored verdict was `APPROVE, 3%, $4.52` regardless — and the PM's own LLM narration said "REJECT... FAIL", directly contradicting the deterministic verdict text it was explicitly instructed not to contradict (`room_prompts.py:104-112`). Fixed: the PM now responds with its own JSON verdict (APPROVE or PASS + size/entry/stop/target, informed by the full debate) instead of narrating around a precomputed action; `enforce_safety_floor()` (previously dead code) wraps it — passes APPROVE through only if `check_mandate_compliance()` clears it, else overrides to REJECT, same as before. `PASS` (declared in the schema, never used) now covers "debate doesn't support entry" without needing a mandate violation. | DEF095 | 2026-07-23 | prompt | backend | **The Trader narrates R:R and drawdown figures nothing checks — and got every one wrong across both live trades in the window.** Saiful: *"check if the llm had done any math in 2 days"*. Measured from `llm_audit` on melehost: **39 calls, all `vllm`, zero errors** — 3 convenes (SCHD + VGK 07-21, INGN 07-22) and 3 Concierge messages. **One-step arithmetic is fine; two-step derived figures failed 4 of 4**, each checked against our own `trading_math` functions, not mental arithmetic. **SCHD** (entry 32.75 / stop 29.60 / target 33.50, size 10%): stop distance *"10% below entry"* → 9.62% ✅; *"~1.0pt to portfolio drawdown"* → 0.962 pt ✅; ***"R:R: 2.5:1"* → implied `risk_reward()` = 0.2:1, 12.5× overstated** on a setup with **2.3% upside against 9.6% downside** — and in the same paragraph the Trader writes *"entering at $32.75 near the $33.5 resistance leaves minimal immediate upside"*, describing the asymmetry correctly and then stating a ratio that contradicts its own sentence. **The PM APPROVED it** at 3.0% and added *"capping portfolio drawdown exposure at ~0.54%"* → actual 0.289 pt, 1.9× overstated. **VGK** (90.00 / 86.50 / 90.75 then 95.00, size 2.0%): *"4% below entry"* → 3.89% ✅; ***"R:R: >2:1"* → 1.4:1** against the $95 target and **0.2:1** against its own first target; ***"~2.5% of portfolio drawdown risk"* → 0.078 pt, 32× overstated**; plus prose *"size conservatively at 2.0%"* against a structured `Size: 0%`. (2) Even when it fires it is telemetry — its own docstring says *"Flag only — the safety floor owns vetoes"* — so a user reads `R:R: 2.5:1` on a 0.2:1 trade unannotated. (3) **The transcript is the contagion vector**: the Trader speaks in EXECUTION, and all three Risk debators plus the PM read its output as `Transcript so far:`, so a wrong ratio becomes the premise the rest of the Room reasons from (the Neutral Debator is already quoting it back). **And the drawdown figure was structurally forced:** `room_prompts.py:201` sets `proposal = trade_proposal if phase in ("RISK","VERDICT") else None` (DEF066), so the Trader is the one agent that proposes levels and **never receives** the derived `drawdown_contribution()` — it had to invent one. **Why it matters:** AMI is a training simulator and R:R is the single number the curriculum teaches users to judge a setup by; the Room presented a 2.3%/9.6% trade as 2.5:1 favourable and approved it, so the user learns the wrong lesson twice — about the trade, and about how to compute R:R. **CR040 degrade-loudly again** — the machinery exists, is wired, and returns `None` on the path that matters. **Proposed fix:** compute derived figures in `trading_math` and inject them the way `_drawdown_snapshot_line()` already does for RISK/VERDICT; extend the coherence check to the Trader and make `stated is None` **on an agent that proposed levels** a flagged condition, not a silent pass; surface incoherence in the transcript rather than in telemetry nobody reads; and per CR038 prefer removing the opportunity — Trader emits levels, the *system* renders every ratio. Sample is small (3 convenes) but it is **every** convene in the window. | DEF110 | 2026-07-26 | prompt | sim | **Stop/target hit marks a sim trade won/lost + stamps realised P&L but never closes the position — the holding persists as phantom shares.** `SimEngine.evaluate_outcomes` (backend/app/services/sim_engine.py) flips a stop/target-hit BUY to `won`/`lost` and sets `realised_pnl = (price − entry) × qty`, but — unlike `manual_close`, which calls `_apply_sell_row` (reduce holding + credit cash) — it does **not** touch `sim_holdings` or `current_cash`. So after a target/stop hit the user still "holds" the shares: they can sell the same position again (double-realise P&L), and `total_value`/`drawdown_pct` are inflated by the phantom position. Confirmed asymmetry (manual close liquidates; auto outcome does not); `test_target_hit_flips_outcome_to_won` only asserts the status flip, never the holding. **Saiful's ruling (2026-07-26): a stop/target hit SHOULD close the position — "it should be closed. we also have alpaca API that we should close it".** Spotted while building CR029-BE (whose lot reconstruction treats won/lost buys as fully-closed — Saiful confirmed that is correct, so CR029 needs no change). **Severity: medium** — sim P&L correctness, user-facing; not a safety-floor breach. **Fix scope (D-5 money/P&L → independent audit gate when built), not yet fixed:** (a) core — `evaluate_outcomes` must liquidate at `closed_price` (mirror `manual_close`'s `_apply_sell_row` + cash proceeds) so the holding is actually reduced, plus the same journal `Closed …` entry; (b) Alpaca — for Alpaca-linked users the close must also propagate to the Alpaca paper account. NOTE: `alpaca_service.py` is link/read-only today (no close/submit-order fn), so (b) needs a new `alpaca_service.close_position` and is a larger sub-scope — likely a separate sub-lane.  **REPRODUCED ON LIVE ALPHA + SEVERITY RAISED (AT:R65, 2026-07-29).** Saiful reported it from the app — *"I don't have many holdings and it is showing older holdings"* — and the production DB confirms it exactly. Query: every `sim_holdings` row joined against the `sim_trades` that produced it. **Three accounts hold phantom shares; one is almost entirely phantom.** User `8f1e288a` shows **6 holdings of which only 1 is real**: AMD 10, HPQ 12, INTC 1, RXT 66 and SPCX 10 all trace to `won`/`lost` trades with ZERO open trades behind them (opened 10–14 Jul, still displayed), while SCHD 6 is the only position with an open trade. It is a **state repair, not a replay**: phantom = `held − (Σ open buys − Σ open sells)`, the same fully-closed rule `cost_basis_lots.py` applies, so it is idempotent — the naive "credit every won/lost trade" shape double-credits on a second run, which on a money column is the worse failure. | DEF114 | 2026-07-27 | prompt | mobile | **The SSE unescape corrupts streamed text on all three surfaces — Room, Brief Your Agent and 1-on-1 — and the shipped decode cannot be fixed by pinning it.** Filed from the CR090-MOBILE auditor's mutation set: **M1** swapped `agent_token`'s order-dependent unescape (`.replaceAll(r'\n','\n')` then `.replaceAll(r'\\',r'\')`) and the suite stayed **green**; **M2** made `done` no longer terminate the generator and the suite stayed **green**. **Architect re-measured 2026-07-27 in real Dart against the actual backend encode and upgraded this from a coverage gap to live corruption:** every sender escapes with `chunk.replace("\\","\\\\").replace("\n","\\n")` (`room.py:213` and `:236`, `one_on_one.py:115`, `brief.py:115`) and every consumer decodes with the same two sequential `replaceAll`s (`api_client.dart:136-137`, `:326`, `:446`) — **two sequential replaceAlls cannot invert that encode in EITHER order**, because the first pass matches across an escape boundary. Measured round-trip: `the token \n means newline` renders as a backslash plus a stray line break, and `C:\next\report` as `C:\` then a newline then `ext\report`; the swapped order (M1) corrupts them differently. Trigger is a backslash immediately followed by `n` — rare in equity prose, not absent (paths, regexes, an agent explaining what `\n` means), and silent when it fires. So M1 is **not** fixable by asserting the current order; the correct decode is a single-pass scanner, verified by the Architect to round-trip **all 13** probe cases exactly (plain newlines, literal `\n`, Windows paths, `a\\b`, trailing backslash, backslash-then-newline, `\\n`, repeated newlines, unicode + emoji, quotes/tabs, empty, lone backslash, `\n\n`). **Fix is CLIENT-ONLY and needs no coordinated release:** the backend pre-escape is redundant (`json.dumps` already escapes) but measured as unsafe to drop while old clients are in the field — it regresses `a\\b`, which round-trips correctly today. Per-chunk decoding is safe because each sender escapes each chunk independently, so no escape sequence spans a chunk boundary. **M2 remains a separate gap**: `streamRoom` builds `http.Client()` inline (`api_client.dart:668`, plus `:301` and `:418`) with no injection point, so "a Room run that never finishes" is untestable until the client is injected. Not introduced by CR090-MOBILE — the auditor diffed every moved case body against `git show main:mobile/lib/services/api/api_client.dart` and found them byte-identical; the refactor preserved behaviour and simply did not back-fill coverage onto already-untested code. Laned to `coder.mobile` at $10, `GATE: independent`. **Fixed 2026-07-27 (coder.mobile round 1):** the two-`replaceAll` pair on all three call sites replaced with one shared `unescapeSseText()` single-pass scanner in `api_client.dart`, round-tripped against the exact backend encode on the Architect's 13-case corpus (`api_client_sse_unescape_test.dart`). `ApiClient` now takes an injectable `http.Client` (D4), routing `streamRoom`/`streamBriefMessage`/`streamOneOnOneMessage` through one shared instance instead of each building its own inline; `done`-terminates-the-generator is now tested on all three surfaces (`api_client_stream_termination_test.dart`), closing M2 too. Both auditor mutations (M1 swapped order, M2 done-doesn't-terminate) demonstrated red, then reverted. Client-only — backend untouched (D2). | DEF119 | 2026-07-27 | backend | api | **`freeze()`'s 2-per-year streak-freeze cap is an unprotected COUNT-then-INSERT — two concurrent requests can both pass the check.** Found by the CR091-STREAKS auditor (track U, independent) as its single MINOR finding; the lane was still voted **COMPLETE round 1** because the blast radius is narrow. `reputation_service.freeze()` enforces the Floor Manager perk's 2/year cap with a `SELECT COUNT(*)` immediately followed by an `INSERT`, with **no `SELECT ... FOR UPDATE` and no constraint spanning "count of rows per user per year."** The only DB constraint is `UniqueConstraint(user_id, frozen_date)` on `StreakFreezeRow`, which prevents re-freezing the *same* date and does nothing for two *different* dates requested concurrently. **The auditor's reproduction was inconclusive and says so:** it seeded one legitimate freeze, opened two uncommitted sessions and called `freeze()` on each for different new dates — both calls got past the stale COUNT before either committed (so the race window is real at the code level), but SQLite's coarse file-level write lock threw `database is locked` on the second insert. That lock is an artifact of the **test engine**, not the application; Postgres's default READ COMMITTED — the actual production engine — does not serialise this. Evidence is therefore structurally reasoned, not mutation-confirmed, and cannot be settled without a live Postgres instance (unavailable: the Mac is a pure editor). Worst case is a paid-tier user obtaining a few extra streak-freeze days per calendar year — **no credits, no money, no security/safety/compliance surface** — which is why this is MINOR rather than a blocker on the lane. Recommended fix: `SELECT ... FOR UPDATE` on the count query, or an equivalent serialising constraint. Note the cap's period is the **calendar year** (`period_key = str(target_date.year)`), confirmed from code during the audit. Line numbers are not a stable identity for a call site. **Found the moment CR098-ROOM rebased onto DEF116:** CR098 added ~146 lines to `room_runner.py`, the same untouched `httpx.get` moved `:2618` → `:2764`, and the guard reported it as a **NEW sync httpx call** — a false positive with no code change behind it. The failure mode matters more than the noise: a guard that fires on innocent line drift is one the next engineer learns to skim past, and the *next* time it fires it will be real. That is strictly worse than no guard — the same reasoning the DEF116 auditor used against the waiver's subtree pruning. **Fix:** pin by **file + count** (`_KNOWN_SYNC_HTTPX_COUNTS`) instead of `file:line`. Movement inside a file is invisible; a genuinely new call still turns it red because the count rises or an unlisted file appears. Line numbers are still *reported* in the failure message for navigation — they are diagnostics, not identity. **Both directions mutation-verified after the fix:** a fresh `httpx.get` in `fundamentals.py` (unlisted file, 0 → 1) fails; a **second** `httpx.get` appended to `revenuecat_client.py` (already-pinned file, 1 → 2) also fails, which is the obvious weakness of count-based pinning and is closed; the CR098 rebase that triggered this now passes clean. The 24 span every dark feature landed since build `0.1.0+55` (2026-07-24) and cluster on three screens: **Portfolio** — `portfolioSectorAllocationHeading`, `portfolioSectorBreach`, `portfolioSectorOtherLabel` (CR026 sector allocation); **Ticker Detail** — the 11 `tickerDetailLot*` / `tickerDetailDividend*` keys (CR029 per-lot cost basis, CR030 dividend chip); **Room console** — `roomLiveDataNoticeTitle`, the four `roomLiveDataFeed*` variants, `roomLiveDataSurchargeCharged`, `roomLiveDataUpgradeCta`, `roomLiveDataTenureUpgradeCta` (CR090 live-data disclosure) and `roomAgentWithheldChairLabel` + `roomAgentWithheldRosterNote` (CR098 withheld chair). **Two are not string swaps and must not be handed over as if they were:** `roomAgentWithheldRosterNote` carries an ICU plural on an `int` (`{days, plural, =1{1 day} other{{days} days}}`) and Arabic has **six** plural categories (`zero`/`one`/`two`/`few`/`many`/`other`) against English's two, so a translator given only the rendered English cannot reconstruct it; and `portfolioSectorBreach` interpolates three placeholders (`{sector}`, `{pct}`, `{limit}`) whose order is not safe to assume under RTL. **Severity is release-scoped, not correctness-scoped:** the locked decision is EN at alpha with AR + MS at v1.0, so nothing here violates the alpha contract — but AR/MS are already selectable in the shipped binary, so every build cut before this closes ships mixed-language UI to anyone who picks one. Verified: key-set diff empty both locales, `flutter gen-l10n` clean, generated `app_localizations_{ar,ms}.dart` show all 6 Arabic plural branches, `flutter test` 143/143. **Still open:** the structural key-set-parity guard — this defect's own point 5 is that translating today's set "just resets the counter" without it; that's a code change outside the i18n lane's scope and needs a coder. **CLOSED 2026-07-28 (AT:R65, `739d085`) — the structural guard is delivered.** `mobile/test/l10n_key_parity_test.dart` fails the build on four distinct divergences, per locale: (1) any key in the template missing from a locale — the defect's own condition; (2) any key a locale defines that the template does not (dead strings, or a rename applied on one side); (3) **placeholder loss** — a translation that drops `{sector}` compiles and then renders a literal brace, which is the risk this row named for `portfolioSectorBreach`; (4) **plural-form loss** — an ICU plural flattened to a plain string in a locale, which is the `roomAgentWithheldRosterNote` risk. **Locales are discovered by globbing `lib/l10n/app_*.arb`, never listed** — a hard-coded list would pass happily the day someone adds `app_fr.arb`, the allowlist-instead-of-invariant shape this codebase keeps re-learning. Two non-vacuity assertions guard the guard: it fails if there are no non-template ARBs to check, and if the template drops below 400 keys. **One design correction worth recording:** the placeholder check first scraped `{name}` out of the strings with a regex and reported a false positive — an ICU plural body (`{days, plural, =1{1 day} other{{days} days}}`) contains braces that are *branch selectors*, and the scraper read `1` as a missing argument. The W3C server-sent-events line-splitting rule terminates a line on **CRLF, LF, *or* a lone CR** — so a bare `\r` inside a `data:` field ends that field for a compliant reader, and `\r\r` produces the blank line that ends the *event*. The exposure is latent, not current — it opens the moment anything else reads these streams (a browser `EventSource`, a proxy that normalises line endings, a curl-based debug script, a future web client). **Why DEF127 deliberately did not fix it:** escaping `\r` to a literal `\\r` would be *rendered* by the shipped `0.1.0+56` decoder, which only inverts `\\n` and `\\\\` — a visible regression in the field to close a hole no live client has. Rejecting is the stronger read: no producer has a legitimate reason to put a carriage return in streamed prose, and a raised error surfaces at the source instead of corrupting a transcript. Either way the whole-tree invariant in `test_def127_sse_framing_invariant.py` extends to cover it, and the escape decision gets a comment saying *why* the two framers differ. (3) The transcript renders through the shared markdown row, so `**bold**` metrics stop reaching users as literal asterisks, and rows gain the metric list and hex avatars. **The guard is the parity test the defect asked for** — `test/widgets/room_board_parity_test.dart` pushes one payload through BOTH mappers and compares a 23-field fingerprint, iterates every wire `VerdictAction` (plus one this build has never shipped) asserting both surfaces agree on outcome, token and neutrality, and asserts the ONLY differences are the three declared ones (the strip, `isRecord`/`recordedAt`, `runId`) so a fourth cannot appear quietly. Tap to retry.` — copy that describes a *transient* fault. A user reads it as a network blip and taps retry, which re-issues the identical malformed request and fails identically, forever. There is no state in which that button can succeed. A second, cheaper guard worth considering: make the retry surface distinguish "request rejected" (4xx — never retryable) from "network failed" (retryable), so a permanently-broken call can never again present as a transient one. **RULED (Saiful, 2026-07-29 0900 check-in): "File it and lane it"** — offered a fix-in-session given the one-line diff and the total outage; he chose standard track-R handling. | DEF157 | 2026-07-29 | prompt | mobile | **A release can ship one store and silently skip the other — `+57` went to TestFlight and never went to Play at all, and nothing anywhere noticed for a week.** Surfaced by Saiful 2026-07-29 as *"we have a drift in the build number for IOS and Android. they should both be 58. android is showing 56"* — reported as a drift in the artifacts, but **measured, the artifacts are not drifted**: `pubspec.yaml` and `android/local.properties` both read `0.1.0+58`, the built APK carries `versionCode 58` (read out of the binary manifest), the AAB is the same build, the melehost tester rig's APK is **byte-identical to the local one by sha256**, TestFlight has `58`, and `google_play_track_version_codes` reports **`internal → [58]`**. The `56` is what was **installed on the device** — Play had not yet propagated the release uploaded minutes earlier. **The real defect is why the gap is TWO builds instead of one:** `+57` was built and uploaded to TestFlight on 2026-07-28 and **was never published to Play**, so Android's last delivered build stayed at `56` while iOS moved to `57` and then `58`. **Mechanism — two independent bump paths with no parity check.** `scripts/build_testflight.sh` and `scripts/build_playstore.sh` each own a `DO_BUMP=1` and each bumps `pubspec.yaml` themselves (`build_testflight.sh:47,86`, `build_playstore.sh:55,87`). Running one without the other advances the shared version for **both** platforms while shipping only one, and nothing in either script, in the promotion protocol, or in any test compares what the two stores actually carry. This is the **P11 shape** — one rule ("both stores ship the same build number") implemented in two places with nothing tying them together — and the **CR040 shape** on top of it: the failure is completely silent, so the only signal is a human noticing a number in the app days later, which is exactly what happened. **Consequence beyond the number:** every Android tester was two builds behind for a week, so any bug report from an Android device in that window was filed against code that was not the code we thought was running — which corrupts triage, not just tidiness. **Second observation from the same measurement, and it is INERT — the first version of this row overstated it and is corrected here.** The Play **closed testing track** (API name `alpha`) holds `versionCode 43` under a release named `ami_trade_release`, against internal's `58`. I initially recorded that as fifteen builds of live staleness and warned that any tester enrolled in closed testing had been running a weeks-old build. **That was wrong, and querying the Play Developer API directly rather than only `google_play_track_version_codes` is what showed it: the release's `status` is `draft`, not `completed`.** A draft release is never served to anyone, whatever the enrolment. So nothing is stale in the field and no tester is stranded — it is an abandoned half-finished release, created around 2026-07-21 when `+43` was current, and left in the console. Consistent with `mobile/android/fastlane/Fastfile`, which has only ever targeted `track: "internal"` (CR048) — our automation has never written to the closed track, so this is a manual console leftover. `beta` and `production` are empty. **Disposition: cosmetic cleanup, not a defect** — discard the draft in the Play Console or leave it; it changes nothing either way. Recorded rather than deleted because the *method* matters: a track-version query alone reports a version code with no indication of whether it is live, which is precisely the kind of number that reads as alarming and is not. **Fix shape (not yet built):** a release must be a single act that either ships both stores or fails loudly. Options in preference order — (1) one `scripts/release.sh` that bumps ONCE and drives both store scripts with `--no-bump`, so the version can only advance when both uploads are attempted, which is how `+58` was in fact shipped by hand today; (2) a parity check that queries `google_play_track_version_codes` and the App Store Connect API for the latest build on each and fails when they differ, runnable standalone so drift is detectable without a release; (3) at minimum, a loud warning in each single-store script that it is advancing a version the other store will not receive. **The guard is the part that matters** and must not be a comment in a runbook: a check that runs, since the whole failure mode here is that a silent skip looks identical to a successful release. **`--no-commit` remains mandatory on `build_testflight.sh`** whenever it is invoked (its `--commit` path does a bare `git commit`, which sweeps a concurrent track's staged work — a separate known trap, not this defect). Relates to **CR040** (degrade loudly — the skip is invisible by construction), **CR048** (which introduced the Play path as a second, parallel pipeline), **`failure_patterns.md` P11** (one rule, N call sites), and the **promotion protocol**, which governs backend rsync to Alpha and says nothing about store parity. **CLOSED 2026-08-06 (AT:R66), Saiful's call: we ship to both stores now.** Practice has changed and is evidenced — `0.1.0+68` went to TestFlight and Play internal in the same session, and the Play side was verified against Google's API rather than an exit code (`google_play_track_version_codes track:internal` → `Found '68' version codes`). **Stated plainly rather than claimed away: this closes on practice, not on a guard.** Nothing structurally prevents a future release reaching one store and not the other; the two publish scripts are still invoked separately and neither checks the other's outcome. If that silence bites again it should be refiled as the guard it wants (one command that ships both and fails if either does not land), not as a reopening of this row. | fixed | — | AT:R65 |

| DEF159 | 2026-07-29 | audit | orchestration | **`gen_registers.py gen` silently publishes another track's *uncommitted* row into the shared committed table, leaving the table's only source file untracked — every clean checkout then fails the drift guard.** Root cause behind REL58 MAJOR M1, and mine. (2) *A green measurement in a dirty shared checkout is not evidence.* The number I handed the auditor was true of my working tree and false of the repository, and nothing in the workflow distinguishes those. **Consequence:** the register guard — the one check that exists to keep the two registers honest — can sit RED on `main` indefinitely while every active session sees green, and the submission that names its test count as evidence is wrong without knowing it. **Fix shape (not built):** (a) `gen` should fail loudly, or at minimum warn, when a row file it consumed is untracked or has unstaged changes — `git ls-files --error-unmatch` per row file is cheap and runs where the generator already walks the directory; degrading loudly here is the whole point (**CR040**). (b) the drift test's failure message should name the offending ID and say "row file missing from the index", which would have made M1 self-diagnosing. (c) the audit-submission convention should require the test count to be measured in a detached worktree, not the shared tree — the auditor already works this way and the architect did not. Binding is guarded by `get(user_id) is None` and deliberately so: its docstring cites re-auth replaying the same `onboarding_session_id`, which without the guard would silently overwrite a mandate the user had since edited. DEF060's `_bind_onboarding_session` guard in `auth.py` is unmodified and re-proven by a re-auth-replay test. **Left `open`, not `fixed`: this is backend-only per the lane fence — the client never sends `restart` today, so the Floor footer control is still a dead end for a signed-in user until a mobile lane threads `restart: true` + the Bearer header through the "Restart onboarding" call site** (likely under `mobile/lib/features/onboarding/` — grep for `readback/confirm` / `ReadbackConfirmRequest`; not opened, per fence). Fixing the call site also required updating two pre-existing tests whose signatures/regexes pinned the old shape: `test/widget_test.dart`'s `_FakeApiClient.confirmReadback` override (caught by `flutter analyze` as an `invalid_override`) and `confirm_restart_onboarding_test.dart`'s DEF152 guard, whose regex pinned the literal `.reset()` — widened to `\.reset\(` so it still proves exactly one call site regardless of arguments. `flutter test`: 398 passed (baseline 393 + 5). `flutter analyze --no-fatal-infos`: 5 known infos, exit 0. | DEF175 | 2026-07-29 | process | orchestration | **A finished lane and an invisible lane look identical from `main` — a worker that commits its hand-off only to its own branch is done, green, pushed, and unseen by both the board and the auditor.** **Third occurrence: CR120, DEF142 (`d5ac6614`), CR112 (`eab8470f`+).** `failure_patterns.md` says the second occurrence of anything earns an entry **with a guard**; instead this has been hand-delivered by the Architect three times, and hand-delivery is the symptom, not the fix. **Mechanism:** `dispatch.sh` derives lane state from files on `main`, and the auditor's watcher globs `orchestration/audit/cr/*.architect.md` on `main`. A coder works in its own worktree on `lane/<ITEM>.<instance>` — correctly, that is the isolation the whole CR052 design rests on — and writes its return file plus the §6 audit bridge **there**. Nothing transports them. So the board reads `ASSIGNED` with no status while a complete, self-verified, pushed lane sits one branch away, and the independent gate never fires because the queue it reads from is empty. **Why it keeps escaping notice:** the failure state is *silence*, and silence is exactly what an unstarted lane looks like too — this is the **CR040** question ("if this fires silently, what does the user end up believing?") applied to the orchestration layer, where the believing party is me. Each time, it was caught only because a human happened to re-read the board and think a number looked wrong. **It also costs money to recover badly:** the DEF142 note records that resuming a worker to write a missing bridge re-pays for its whole accumulated context, which is how a CR120 resume burned a $3 cap — so the recovery path is Architect hand-transport, which is precisely the manual step that should not exist. **Fix shape — the guard must RUN, not be a line in the protocol:** `dispatch.sh inbox` should scan `origin/lane/*` for any branch carrying a `STATUS: READY_FOR_*` return file or an `<ITEM>.architect.md` that `main` does not have, and report it (exit 1, matching the existing "integrate first" convention). Secondary options: have `dispatch_launch.sh`'s task body require the hand-off be cherry-picked to `main` as its final act, or teach the auditor's watcher to glob lane branches as well as `main` — but the inbox check is the cheapest and is the only one that catches a worker that died before its last step. **Transport must stay verbatim when it does happen** — the hand-off is the builder's account, and the Architect delivering it must not become the Architect rewriting it. Mutation-proven both directions: hiding a live lane's hand-off makes it fire, restoring it clears. **Scoped to lanes not yet `DISPATCH: ACCEPTED`** — the unscoped first version reported CR087-BE, CR087-MOBILE and DEF114, all merged and closed months ago, which would have been permanently red and never actionable; the scoping is what keeps the section worth reading. | DEF191 | 2026-07-30 | audit | backend | **The four-leg invariant guard is a hand-written checklist, not a guard — a new enforced-limit field that nobody remembers to add to it passes vacuously.** `test_cr101_be1_settable_risk_caps.py::test_every_enforced_limit_field_is_enforced_disclosed_and_settable` was written in CR101-BE1 as *the* mechanism that stops the "settable but unenforced" class recurring — the CR101 row calls it "the check that stops this recurring, and it is what CR101 exists for as much as the fields are." It enumerates its subjects **by hand**. **Measured one CR later:** CR101-BE2 added five new enforced-limit fields (`post_loss_cooldown_hours`, `max_open_positions`, `max_trades_per_day`, `max_trades_per_week`, `max_open_risk_pct`) and the guard picked up none of them — the builder had to append five blocks manually, and disclosed it rather than let it pass silently. **The guard failed its own purpose on the very next change**, which is the `failure_patterns.md` **P12** class recurring inside the file written to catch P12. **The failure mode is worse than having no guard:** a developer who adds a field and forgets the checklist gets a **green suite** containing a test whose name asserts universality — `every_enforced_limit_field` — while its body covers a frozen list. That is a positive, misleading signal, not a missing one. **Fix needs a design decision, which is why this is a row and not a patch:** the guard must *derive* its subject list from the schema instead of restating it — a class-level registry of enforced-limit fields, or a `Field(json_schema_extra={"enforced_limit": True})` marker, with the test iterating `Mandate.model_fields` and failing on any marked field missing a leg. Either shape converts the rule into "you cannot add an enforced limit without declaring it," which is the make-it-structural discipline this project already applies elsewhere (CR038: prompt instructions are not controls — conventions are not controls either). **Until fixed, the guard's green is evidence about the listed fields only, never about the schema.** Note this is a *different* defect from the CR101-BE2 round-1 architect BLOCKER (three limits silently unenforced on the Room path): that one is missing enforcement, this one is the missing detector that should have made it impossible — and neither the guard nor the suite caught the other. Surfaced by the CR101-BE2 builder under its assign's instruction to say so if BE1's guard did not auto-pick-up the new fields. Relates to **CR101-BE1** (wrote the guard), **CR101-BE2** (found the gap), **DEF187**, `failure_patterns.md` **P11/P12**, **CR046**. **BE-GUARD191 (2026-07-30):** the subject list is now derived — `Mandate.enforced_limit_field_names()` walks `Mandate.model_fields` for a `Field(json_schema_extra={"enforced_limit": True})` marker (picked over a class-level registry so the declaration sits next to the field), and the guard test fails naming any derived field with no registered four-leg probe; vacuity (derivation finds nothing) also fails. Proven live: a throwaway marked field with no probe turns the suite red naming it; reverted after. **Acceptance 4 (the harder half) is a disclosed PARTIAL, left `open`:** a second test, `test_no_unmarked_numeric_field_is_referenced_by_enforcement_code`, greps a fixed list of enforcement-adjacent files for a literal `mandate.<field>` read and flags an unmarked numeric field found there — proven live the same way (an unmarked field referenced from `safety_floor.py` turns it red). This catches a developer who implements enforcement in the usual places and forgets the marker, which is every existing enforced limit's shape. It does **not** catch a field wired through a mechanism that never spells `mandate.<name>` in one of those files (dict-keyed access off `model_dump()`, a local-variable alias, enforcement added to a file outside the fixed list) — no mechanism here closes that gap, so the class this DEF exists to catch (a developer who forgets BOTH the marker and reads the field unconventionally) is not fully closed. **FIXED 2026-08-06 (AT:R66) — acceptance 4 closed by changing the question.** The residual gap was real and not narrowable: `test_no_unmarked_numeric_field_is_referenced_by_enforcement_code` searches CODE, and a code search cannot be complete — this row's own disclaimer lists three ways round it (`model_dump()` read by key, aliased to a local before use, enforcement in a file outside the 7-entry `_ENFORCEMENT_ADJACENT_SOURCE_FILES`). Widening the file list or the regex shrinks the gap without closing it, because the set of ways to READ a field is unbounded. **The set of FIELDS is not.** `test_every_numeric_mandate_field_is_classified_as_a_limit_or_explicitly_not` asks the bounded question instead: every numeric field on `Mandate` must be either marked `enforced_limit` (which drags in the four-leg probe requirement) or listed in `_NON_LIMIT_NUMERIC_FIELDS` with a reason. | DEF212 | 2026-08-03 | audit | backend | **R0's breach-weight ceiling is one-sided: a sub-0.1-precision mandate cap can still render equal to the weight breaching it.** Found by the independent auditor as MINOR `m2` on the CR136-M05 round-2 verdict (`0f220f71`), after round 1's MAJOR M2 (the demonstrated 35.04→"35.0" case) was closed and mutation-proven. Auditor's reproduction: `cap=35.05 true_weight=35.06 → shown cap "35.1", shown weight "35.1"`; `cap=39.95 true_weight=39.96 → both "40.0"`. The §F5 sentence then asserts a breach while displaying two equal numbers — the same shown-vs-enforced contradiction R0 exists to remove, one precision level down. **Not reachable from any shipped preset**, which is why it graded MINOR and did not bounce the lane: `DEFAULT_RISK_TIER_CAPS = {1: 1.5, 2: 1.5, 3: 3.0, 4: 4.5, 5: 4.5}` and the sector presets (25.0–60.0) are all exact at 1 dp, so a weight strictly above them always ceilings a display unit higher. Reaching it needs a deliberate sub-0.1 override, which nothing currently prevents: both `single_name_cap_pct` and `sector_cap_pct` are plain `float | None` (`schemas/mandate.py:162-163`) with no `ge`/`le`/`multiple_of` constraint, and the PATCH path (`api/mandate.py:134-148`) narrates the change without validating precision. **FIXED 2026-08-06 (AT:R66) — framing (a), unblocked by M06's lane closing COMPLETE.** Three framings were on the table: (a) escalate precision on both numbers when they render equal (auditor's preferred, but it spans `portfolio_rules.py` AND M06's `portfolio_finding.py`, which could not be touched while that lane was open at round 1); (b) floor the displayed cap to 1 dp — rejected on inspection, since showing "35.0%" for an enforced 35.05% cap is itself a shown-vs-enforced mismatch, merely a smaller one; (c) constrain the schema so sub-0.1 caps cannot be stored — cleanest under CR040's "make it impossible" rule but a mandate-schema change with migration implications, and it belongs to whoever owns that surface. Took (a). **Where it lives is the part worth recording:** the escalation is in the RENDERER (`portfolio_finding._breach_display`), not the rule engine, because a validator test mutates `cap_pct` on a real rule result and expects the sentence to follow — moving rendering into `portfolio_rules.py` would have left that test passing while asserting nothing. The rule engine instead carries one new fact, `weight_pct_raw` (the un-ceilinged weight), so the renderer can separate the pair without re-rounding a number that was already rounded once. `_breach_display` walks dp 1→6, ceilinging the weight and half-up-ing the cap at each step, and returns the first pair that differs: the weight is never shown below the true one, the cap never shown stricter than enforced, and the direction of the breach is preserved. **`build_allowlist` calls the same function** rather than reproducing its ladder — the allow-list's own breach registration stops at 2 dp, so a pair separating at 3 would have rendered a token the validator then rejects, throwing away the Finding for containing its own §F5 line. Tests: a 3-case parametrized pin (both auditor reproductions plus a pair that needs 3 dp) asserting inequality, direction, and that neither number crossed the truth; plus an allow-list admission test. Mutation-verified: collapsing `_BREACH_MAX_DP` to 1 kills all 4, and the backstop logs `portfolio_finding_breach_display_unseparated` rather than failing silently. | DEF213 | 2026-08-03 | audit | backend | **A non-contiguous joined return grid is annualised as if it were daily, so a book containing one gappy holding reports an overstated volatility — silently, with no flag of any kind.** Raised by the architect as "Attack 2" in the CR136-M04 audit lane and confirmed by the auditor at round 1 as "real and correctly reasoned", but graded by neither, both declining to state a severity off a direction with no number attached. Measured 2026-08-03 (scripts preserved in the CR136 audit pack: `attack2_measure.py`, `attack2_sweep.py`, `attack2_realistic.py`). **Mechanism:** `_join` (`portfolio_health.py:302-307`) intersects dates across the holdings and the benchmark; `_returns_on` (`:186-190`) then takes consecutive close-to-close ratios *on that joined grid*, so a return spanning k trading days is treated as one daily observation; `annualize_vol` (`trading_math/portfolio_risk.py:36`) multiplies by √252 unconditionally. Nothing checks `window_days` against `n_observations`, though the engine computes and publishes both in every block. **Boundary case, 24 independent paths, one underlying price process observed two ways:** thinning to every other trading day overstates σ by **1.372× on the even-day grid and 1.424× on the odd-day grid (mean; min 1.207, max 1.614; 24/24 seeds overstated)** — √2 = 1.414 is the prediction if every joined return spans exactly two days. Re-annualising the same thinned estimate at 126 periods/year instead of 252 returns **0.970 (sd 0.060, straddling 1.0)**, which localises the entire gap in the annualisation constant rather than anything about the path. Absolute: **+7.68pp mean (min +4.65pp, max +10.27pp)** on a book whose true σ is ~20%. **Realistic case — one thinly-traded holding of three, the other two and the benchmark complete, 12 paths per level:** 5% of that one holding's days missing overstates portfolio σ by **+6.1%**, 10% by **+7.9%**, 20% by **+12.5%**, 40% by **+29.8%**. **At every level `dropped_holdings` is empty, `partial` is false, and `sufficient` is true** — the engine reports a clean, confident measurement, so this is invisible to the user, to the card and to the journal. That silence is what makes it a defect rather than an estimator limitation: one holding's feed quality degrades every metric in the book (σ, DR², risk contributions, the typical-bad-month figure derived from σ, and the R1/R3 rule firings M05 gates on them), and nothing says so. **FIXED 2026-08-03 — the loud half, per Saiful's call "guard now, correct later".** The engine already computed both numbers and published them in every block; it simply never compared them. It does now: `window_days / n_observations` above the new `GRID_DENSITY_MAX` sets `insufficient_cause: sparse_grid` on every Σ-derived block, so a grid the √252 annualisation does not fit produces no number at all rather than a confident wrong one. The card carries pinned copy for it (`Price history available to AMI's engine has gaps: {n} trading days spread across {days} calendar days.`) — the generic body would have been true but reads as a limit of the user's book, and this is a limit of the feed. **Threshold derivation** (`def213_guard_threshold.py`, measured 2026-08-03): the gappy side was already measured above; the CLEAN side is not 7/5 = 1.40 on a real calendar, because market holidays remove trading days without removing calendar days. 10y of daily bars across 8 instruments, both venues, four asset classes — all 8 share ONE calendar (2513 of 2513 dates, so a clean book's join loses nothing for calendar reasons) — gives mean 1.4535 and **max 1.4921** over 11,038 rolling windows at every length the engine consumes. Yahoo's free endpoint caps that ticker at ~10y today, so 9/11 and Sandy are outside the fetchable window and the multi-day-closure tail is **constructed, not observed**: deleting L consecutive sessions from the real calendar reproduces the shape, worst **1.5556 at L=5**, longer than any US closure since 1933. **1.65** clears that by 6.1% and the observed max by 10.6%, and fires above 11.9% of one holding's days missing — just past the point where the bias overtakes the estimator's own error bar (F17: 6.29–6.37% relative at T=126), so below the line a gap costs less than the sampling noise the metric already carries. Six mutations killed, including the one that mattered: tightening the threshold to 1.45 initially SURVIVED, because the false-fire test used the weekday-only synthetic grid (ratio exactly 1.40) and so held for any threshold above 1.40 — a guard that only holds on a calendar the market does not use. The clean-book test now reproduces both measured densities exactly and the mutation dies at 1.45, 1.50 and 1.55. `short_window` is checked first and wins, so a young book is never told its feed has holes. **Closed as filed, and the filed defect was the SILENCE** — `dropped_holdings` empty, `partial` false, `sufficient` true on a book overstated 29.8%. The estimator still assumes 252 below the threshold; annualising by the grid's realised period length, which arm D shows recovers the true figure, is **CR139**, along with the M05 threshold re-calibration it forces and the re-derivation of `GRID_DENSITY_MAX` itself. Read `done` here as "no longer silent", not as "the annualisation is now right". | fixed | [backend/app/services/portfolio_health.py](../../backend/app/services/portfolio_health.py) | AT:R66 |

| DEF215 | 2026-08-04 | promotion | backend | **`init_schema()` creates new tables on an EXISTING database without stamping Alembic, so the first migration that CREATEs one of them dies on `DuplicateTable` and every migration after it in the chain silently never runs.** Found live during CR136's first promotion to Alpha (`alpha-2026-08-04-1`), and it took the journal down for real users. **Mechanism, verified in the code:** `init_schema` (`backend/app/db/session.py:86-126`) calls `Base.metadata.create_all(engine)` at `:104` and only *then* checks `if "alembic_version" in inspector.get_table_names(): return` at `:117-118`. That guard protects the **stamp**, not the **create_all** above it. On a fresh DB the pair is coherent — create_all builds everything, the self-stamp records it, and `alembic upgrade head` is a clean no-op, which is what the docstring and `/promote-to-alpha` step 6's note both describe. On an **existing** DB `create_all` still fires and builds exactly the tables that are missing — i.e. every table the incoming CR just added — and then returns without stamping, because `alembic_version` is present. Alembic is now behind reality with no record of it. **Measured on Alpha 2026-08-04:** the recreated container's first DB touch built `price_history_daily` and `portfolio_value_snapshots` (both complete — right columns, unique constraints, indexes, FK — because create_all reads the same `Base.metadata` the migrations were autogenerated from); `alembic_version` stayed at `8a4ce4f8abc3`; `alembic upgrade head` then reported `Running upgrade 8a4ce4f8abc3 -> a9b0c1d20026` and raised `psycopg2.errors.DuplicateTable: relation "price_history_daily" already exists`. **The damage was not the table it failed on.** Alembic aborts the whole chain, so `c2d3e4f50028` and `d3e4f5a60029` — which ALTER `journal_entries`, a table `create_all` will never touch because it already exists — never ran. The promoted code maps `JournalEntryRow.dedupe_key`, the column was absent, and **every journal read on live Alpha failed**: `ProgrammingError (psycopg2.errors.UndefinedColumn) column journal_entries.dedupe_key does not exist`. 1203 journal rows were intact throughout; this was schema, not data. **That is the shape worth remembering: a create-table migration failing masked an ALTER the running code depended on, so the outage surfaced in an unrelated, already-shipped feature rather than in the new one.** Nothing in the promotion protocol would have caught it — step 6 runs `alembic upgrade head` and its own note says the self-stamp makes this "a clean no-op on a fresh container", which is true and reads as though it covers the case it does not. **Resolved by hand at promotion time** (Saiful's call, fix forward over rollback): `alembic stamp b1c2d3e40027` then `alembic upgrade head`, after verifying both created tables matched their migrations column-for-column so the stamp was a fact rather than an assumption. Journal reads restored, `uq_journal_dedupe` confirmed as `CREATE UNIQUE INDEX ... WHERE (deleted_at IS NULL)`, head at `d3e4f5a60029`. **FIXED 2026-08-06 (AT:R66) — both halves, because the candidates were not alternatives.** The filed options (a) *run migrations before the app's first DB touch* and (b) *skip `create_all` when `alembic_version` exists* address different halves of the same outage, and doing only one leaves the other live. (c) — re-stamping to head after `create_all` — stays rejected: it papers over a genuinely divergent schema. **(b), the wedge.** The presence check moved ABOVE `create_all` in `init_schema` (`session.py`), so on any database carrying `alembic_version` this function now creates nothing at all and Alembic owns the schema outright; `create_all` reverts to what it is actually for, which is a fresh sqlite tempfile fixture. The lazy-call shape mattered here: `init_schema()` is called from ~10 store constructors, not once at boot, so "first DB touch" is whatever request lands first — the new short-circuit is keyed on the engine OBJECT (`_schema_checked_for is engine`) so repeated calls cost nothing and `reset_for_tests`, which builds a new engine, re-arms it for free without needing its own reset line. **(a), the window.** `/promote-to-alpha` step 5 now builds the image and runs `docker compose run --rm --no-deps api-alpha alembic upgrade head` against the live DB **while the OLD container is still serving**, and only swaps containers if that succeeds; step 6 demoted from "run migrations" to "confirm `alembic current` reports head". Verified the image has `CMD` and no `ENTRYPOINT`, so the command override actually takes. Step 6's old note — which said the self-stamp made this "a clean no-op on a fresh container" — was true and read as though it covered the case it did not; rewritten with the outage described in place. **Plus the thing that would have made it cheap to diagnose:** `_report_if_behind_head` logs `db_schema_behind_head` with both `current_revision` and `head_revision` when the DB is behind the code, and deliberately never raises — a boot that refuses on a bad read would convert a reporting problem into an outage. **Tests** (`test_def215_schema_ownership.py`, 4): a table `Base.metadata` knows about and the DB lacks must STAY missing when `alembic_version` is present; the fresh-DB non-vacuity case still builds AND stamps; the behind-head report names both revisions; a DB at head reports nothing (noise is how the next real one gets scrolled past). | DEF220 | 2026-08-06 | audit | backend | **Six check-then-INSERT sites under a real uniqueness constraint have no `IntegrityError` handler — surfaced by widening the P15 guard, none of them reviewed.** `failure_patterns.md` P15 says a function that SELECTs what exists and INSERTs the rest is correct in one process and raises in two. The guard written for it initially matched call sites **by name** (`upsert_*`), which CR136-M01's round-2 auditor showed enforces a naming convention rather than the pattern: their `AUD-M4` added an unguarded check-then-`session.add` that simply was not called `upsert_*`, and the guard passed. **Widened to the shape** — any function that both reads a model and `session.add`s that same model, where the model carries a `UniqueConstraint`, a unique `Index`, a `unique=True` column, or a **primary key with no default** (the natural-key case, which collides exactly like an explicit constraint; a uuid4-defaulted PK cannot collide and is excluded, which is what keeps the rule from flagging every append-only insert). **What it found, first run:** 21 collidable models, 9 matching sites. One guarded in place (`portfolio_snapshot.py`, M03's original), two guarded at the caller (`price_history.upsert_daily_bars` and `ticker_reference.upsert_reference`, both fixed under CR136-M01 A2 — the handler wraps the call because the commit happens in the caller's `get_session().__exit__`, which is precisely the frame this AST rule cannot see from inside the callee). **The remaining six are unreviewed and are this defect:** `auth_service._upsert_user_device` → `UserDeviceRow`; `lessons_service._check_agent_unlocks` → `AgentActivationRow`; `mandate_store.upsert` → `MandateRow`; `overlay_store.save_new_version` → `OverlayEditCounter`; `reputation_service._award_badge` → `BadgeRow`; `social_context._cache_write` → `SocialSentimentCacheRow`. **Not fixed blind, deliberately.** Each needs its own reachability question answered before a handler is added, and the answers will differ: `_award_badge` and `_check_agent_unlocks` are idempotent-by-intent (a badge awarded twice is a skip), `_cache_write` is a cache whose loser can simply drop the write, and `mandate_store.upsert` writes user-authored state where silently swallowing a lost race could hide a real conflict. Wrapping all six in the same `except IntegrityError: pass` would satisfy the guard and answer none of those questions — the CR040 shape, and the reason P15 asks the handler to **say which outcome it chose**. **Severity is deliberately not higher.** No live failure is known; the same in-process accident that hid CR136-M01's instance (one uvicorn, no `--workers`) covers these too, and CR136-M01's auditor measured **0 races in 60 trials** on this stack. That protection is a deployment fact, not a guard, and CLAUDE.md's Beta stack is **GCP Cloud Run** — instances share no state, so every one of these becomes reachable the day a second instance exists. **Held from regressing meanwhile:** the six are pinned in `_UNREVIEWED` inside `backend/tests/unit/test_p15_check_then_insert_guard.py`, so a **seventh** site fails the build immediately, and a pin left behind after a fix also fails (a stale entry hides the next real one). The pin is exact rather than a floor on purpose — P6b warns against exact pins on data designed to grow, and this is the opposite case. **FIXED 2026-08-15 (AT:R70) — six sites, THREE different answers, which is the whole point.** Each got the outcome its own reachability question produced, exactly as this row demanded, and the spread is the evidence that a blanket `except IntegrityError: pass` would have been wrong: **(1) re-read and update** — `_upsert_user_device` and the overlay edit counter, because their loser still has a change to apply. The device row's `user_id` **re-keys on claim adoption**, so a loser that skips leaves the device owned by the pre-claim anonymous account until some later bootstrap happens to win; the counter feeds `can_edit`, i.e. the Floor Pass lifetime cap, where a dropped increment is a free edit and a double-count charges one never spent. **(2) retry once, then RAISE** — `mandate_store.upsert` and `overlay_store.save_new_version`, which hold text the user wrote. A retry is not a fudge: the version is a per-user sequence, not a lock, so landing the loser at N+2 is byte-identical to the two requests arriving a millisecond apart. What must not exist is a silent third outcome, so a second collision raises a **named** `MandateVersionConflictError` / `OverlayVersionConflictError` rather than looping — "your edit did not land" has to be distinguishable from any other database error. **(3) skip** — `_award_badge` and `_cache_write`, idempotent by intent. **Two things this row did not know, both found by reading rather than by the guard failing.** **(a) `_upsert_user_device`'s docstring asserted the opposite of the truth** — *"UNIQUE on device_install_id keeps this safe under races"*. The constraint is what makes the second writer RAISE; it was the hazard, described as the mitigation. **(b) The six were never six.** `overlay_store.save_new_version` contains **two** collidable inserts, and the guard could only see one: `OverlayEditCounter` is constructed inline inside `add()`, while `UserOverlayRow` binds to `new_row` first — and the rule only recognised the inline form. Both are fixed here; the rule's blind spot (12 of 20 sites invisible, measured) is widened here and its 11 newly-visible sites are pinned and filed as **DEF308**, not fixed blind — this row's own discipline applied to its own overflow. **Every handler uses a SAVEPOINT (`begin_nested`), never a bare flush**, following `career_ledger.post_career_event`'s established pattern, and the placement is load-bearing in two places: `_award_badge` runs inside `_grant_milestone`'s transaction **carrying a credit grant**, so a poisoned session would let a cosmetic badge race destroy monetized state; and `_check_agent_unlocks`'s SAVEPOINT is **inside** its per-agent loop, so one collision cannot roll back the other agents unlocked in the same pass. **A vestigial second version probe was deleted** from `save_new_version` — the retry loop recomputes it, and leaving both would have been one derivation reading stale while the other retried (DEF098 in miniature). It was not cosmetic: it silently absorbed a test's fault injection and made a mutation survive. **Guarded by 8 new tests** in `backend/tests/unit/test_def220_check_then_insert_outcomes.py`, one per outcome, and they exist because the P15 guard is a **source** rule that cannot tell a correct handler from `pass`. **The collisions are real, not mocked**: a session proxy blinds the pre-check SELECT once — a faithful reproduction of P15's read-to-commit gap — and the INSERT then meets the genuine constraint. Threads were rejected as the mechanism for the reason this defect was invisible in the first place: the auditor measured 0 races in 60 trials because one uvicorn holds an invariant nobody wrote down, so a thread test would be flaky-green. **Mutation-proved 7/7** (device handler → `pass`; mandate version derivation reverted; counter handler → `pass`; badge SAVEPOINT → bare flush; overlay retry → single attempt; unlock SAVEPOINT hoisted out of the loop; cache handler reverted to the broad `except`). **Three of those seven initially SURVIVED and the tests were rewritten rather than the claim softened** — the counter and overlay tests were exercising the else-branch instead of the handler, and the unlock test had built its own `begin_nested()` inline, so it was asserting SQLAlchemy rather than our code, which is precisely what CLAUDE.md says not to write. The unlock test is now an explicit structural pin on the SAVEPOINT's placement inside the loop, with the reason it is not raced stated in the test itself. **The social-cache fix is about the LOG, not the row**: an `except Exception` already swallowed that collision, so "no crash, one row" was true before the change and would have proved nothing — what was wrong is that a benign lost race logged `social_cache_write_failed` at **WARN**, a warning that fires when the system is working correctly, which is how an operator learns to scroll past the line (DEF277/DEF300's class). | fixed | [backend/tests/unit/test_def220_check_then_insert_outcomes.py](../../backend/tests/unit/test_def220_check_then_insert_outcomes.py) · [backend/app/services/overlay_store.py](../../backend/app/services/overlay_store.py) · [backend/app/services/mandate_store.py](../../backend/app/services/mandate_store.py) | AT:R70 |
| DEF221 | 2026-08-06 | promotion | mobile | **The iOS app declares `MinimumOSVersion 13.0`, and from Spring 2027 Apple refuses to accept an upload below 15.0 — so this is a hard deadline on the ability to ship at all, not a compatibility preference.** Surfaced by App Store Connect during CR136's `0.1.0+68` TestFlight upload (checklist 3.1), verbatim: *"This app has a MinimumOSVersion of 13.0. Starting in Spring 2027, all iOS apps must have a MinimumOSVersion of 15.0 or later in order to be uploaded to App Store Connect or submitted for distribution."* The upload itself **succeeded** — today it is a warning. **Why it is filed rather than fixed on the spot.** Raising the floor drops iOS 13/14 devices, which is a product decision about who we are willing to lose, not a build-settings edit: the iPhone 6s/7 generation tops out at iOS 15, so the practical loss is narrower than it sounds, but it is still a decision Saiful owns and it wants a number (App Store Connect's own analytics can give the installed-base split once there is one). **The trap is the deadline's shape.** Nothing degrades gradually — the app keeps building, keeps uploading, and keeps working right up until an Apple-side cutoff after which **no build can be uploaded at all**, including an emergency fix. A team that discovers this in Spring 2027 discovers it while trying to ship something urgent. That is the same class as the config-gated failures CR040 exists for: nothing goes red until the moment it matters. **Second warning from the same upload, recorded here rather than filed separately because it is one line of build config and no deadline attaches to it:** the archive carried no dSYM for `objective_c.framework` (UUID `1C430BBE-F1B9-31FC-8443-4B75665A5817`), so symbol upload failed and any crash inside that framework will arrive unsymbolicated in Sentry — a debugging cost, not a user-facing one. **Fix, not yet made:** decide the floor (15.0 is the minimum that satisfies the rule; 16.0 or 17.0 buys more headroom before the next ratchet), set `IPHONEOS_DEPLOYMENT_TARGET` in `mobile/ios/` and the matching `platform :ios` in the Podfile, then re-run the store builds and confirm the warning is gone. Wants the decision recorded with the installed-base number that justified it, so the next ratchet is a re-run of a known argument rather than a fresh one. **FIXED 2026-08-06 (AT:R66). Saiful's floor decision: 16.0, not the 15.0 minimum.** **The number the row asked for, measured** — our own iOS fleet, read from OneSignal: **3 devices, all on iOS 26.5+** (Simulator 26.5, `iPhone18,1` 26.5.2, `iPhone13,2` 26.5.2). Stated honestly: n=3 and they are internal test devices, so this is not an installed-base measurement — it is "there is no user to lose yet", which is the cheapest moment this decision will ever be made. **What made 16.0 the choice rather than 15.0:** iOS 13, 14 and 15 share the same hardware floor (iPhone 6s and later, per Apple's published support matrix), so 13→15 drops ZERO devices and only sheds users sitting on a five-year-old OS by choice — but Apple has ratcheted this requirement repeatedly, so 15.0 buys compliance and a repeat of this decision. 16.0 costs the iPhone 6s/7/SE1 generation (2015-16 hardware, ~11 years old by the time the deadline lands) and buys headroom past the next ratchet. **Nothing in the dependency graph was forcing or blocking either number** — before the change the pods resolved to 13.0 or lower, so this was purely a product call. **Applied:** `IPHONEOS_DEPLOYMENT_TARGET = 16.0` at all 3 sites in `project.pbxproj`, `platform :ios, '16.0'` in the Podfile, and a `post_install` hook that pins every pod target to the same floor rather than letting each drift to its own podspec minimum — after `pod install`, **all 174 pod build configurations read 16.0** (before: a spread of 9.0/10.0/11.0/12.0/13.0). **Second half fixed in the same pass:** the `post_install` hook now sets `DEBUG_INFORMATION_FORMAT = dwarf-with-dsym` on Release and Profile, so the missing `objective_c.framework` dSYM that failed symbol upload on `0.1.0+68` is emitted and crashes there reach Sentry symbolicated. **Verified by building**, not by inspection: `flutter build ios --release --no-codesign` → `Xcode build done. 82.7s` / `Built build/ios/iphoneos/Runner.app (58.9MB)`, exit 0. The ASC warning itself can only be confirmed gone on the next store upload, which is the one claim left unmade here. **CORRECTION 2026-08-06, measured on the `0.1.0+69` upload: the floor half is fixed, the dSYM half is NOT, and this row's claim that it was is wrong.** The floor is confirmed — the built app reports `MinimumOSVersion 16.0` / `CFBundleVersion 69` from its own Info.plist, and the Spring-2027 rejection warning did not appear in the upload. But the dSYM warning came back **verbatim, same UUID** (`1C430BBE-F1B9-31FC-8443-4B75665A5817`). **Why the fix could not have worked:** the `post_install` hook iterates `installer.pods_project.targets`, and `objective_c` is **not a CocoaPods target at all** — it is a Dart FFI package (`pubspec.lock`, built through the native-assets / `native_toolchain_c` pipeline), so nothing in the Podfile reaches it. | DEF224 | 2026-08-06 | promotion | infra | **SSH key auth to melehost stopped working mid-session, so the automated-tester APK is now STALE and every ops path that needs a shell is blocked.** Surfaced by `publish_playstore.sh`, which uploaded `0.1.0+69` to the Play internal track successfully and then failed its own APK refresh: `✗ scp FAILED — automated-tester APK is STALE at saiful@192.168.20.59:/home/saiful/hermes_folder/project/AMI_MarketApps/apk/`. The script reported it loudly rather than exiting 0 on a half-success, which is the CR040 behaviour working. **Diagnosed, not guessed:** `ssh -v melehost` establishes the TCP connection, negotiates with `OpenSSH_10.2p1 Ubuntu`, offers `/Users/saiful/.ssh/id_ed25519 ED25519 SHA256:gPSB8flodYZbgKMsvyYZeLPnhKj8ASQhMrKiTdiFFXI` and gets `Permission denied (publickey,password)`. So the host is up, the network is fine, the key file is present and readable, and the SERVER is rejecting the key. Not an agent problem: `~/.ssh/config` sets `IdentitiesOnly yes` with an explicit `IdentityFile`, so the empty `ssh-add -l` is irrelevant, and `ssh-add --apple-load-keychain` changed nothing. **The timeline is the useful part:** SSH worked repeatedly during this session's promotion — rsync, `alembic upgrade head`, healthcheck polling, `psql` queries, `docker logs`, and the OneSignal diagnostics all succeeded — and stopped some time between the post-promotion index verification and the Play publish ~40 minutes later. **Nothing in that window touched melehost**: the promotion rsync targets `~/ami_trade/` and cannot reach `~/.ssh`, and the intervening work was all local (the DEF222 Flutter fix and the TestFlight build). Most likely server-side: an `authorized_keys` change, an sshd restart with new config, a full disk preventing the file being read, or a fail2ban ban. **Deliberately stopped retrying** rather than hammering the endpoint, since repeated failures are exactly what would deepen a ban. **Alpha itself is UNAFFECTED and verified so** — `/v1/health` returns `{"status":"ok",...,"env":"staging"}` and `/v1/sim/quote/AAPL` returns 200 over the Cloudflare tunnel, which does not use SSH. This is an admin-access outage, not a service outage. **What it blocks:** the Hermes UAT rig is testing a stale APK (`+68` behaviour against a `+69` release, so any report it files is about old code); the DEF201 janitor cron cannot be wired; and no further Alpha diagnosis or promotion is possible until access is restored. **Needs Saiful** — console or password access to melehost to inspect `~/.ssh/authorized_keys`, `sshd` status, disk free, and any fail2ban jail. **Re-probed 2026-08-07 — still refused, and the extra evidence narrows it sharply.** Host reachable (`ping` 2/2, 0% loss, ~7 ms — it is on the LAN), port 22 open (`nc -z` succeeded), local keypair intact and self-consistent (private and `.pub` both `SHA256:gPSB8flodYZbgKMsvyYZeLPnhKj8ASQhMrKiTdiFFXI`, comment `melehost`). **The host key is UNCHANGED** — `ssh-keygen -F 192.168.20.59` finds it in `known_hosts` and ssh raised no mismatch warning, so this is the same machine, not a reimage. All three local identities (`id_ed25519`, `id_ed25519_nvidia`, `id_rsa_ami_webserver`) are rejected identically. **The rejection is CLEAN and at the protocol level** — sshd accepts the connection, reads its config, receives the offered key and answers `Permission denied (publickey,password)`. That argues AGAINST a fail2ban block, which drops or times the connection out rather than completing a key exchange and declining. Stopped probing after five total attempts rather than risk creating the ban we do not currently have. **So the surviving causes are all server-side, in roughly this order:** (1) `~/.ssh/authorized_keys` truncated, replaced or its permissions/ownership broken — sshd silently refuses a key when the file, `~/.ssh`, or `$HOME` is group- or world-writable, which is the classic cause and produces exactly this error; (2) an `sshd_config` change (`PubkeyAuthentication no`, an `AllowUsers`/`AllowGroups` narrowing, or a `Match` block); (3) a full disk preventing `authorized_keys` being read; (4) the `saiful` account itself disabled, expired or renamed — a nonexistent user produces an identical message. **The way back in, and it does not need physical console:** the server advertises `password` as an accepted method, so `ssh saiful@192.168.20.59` with the account password should still work. Once in, the diagnosis is four commands: `ls -la ~/ ~/.ssh ~/.ssh/authorized_keys` (expect `$HOME` and `~/.ssh` NOT group-writable, `authorized_keys` 600), `sudo tail -50 /var/log/auth.log` (sshd states the exact refusal reason there — 'Authentication refused: bad ownership or modes' is the giveaway for cause 1), `df -h /` for cause 3, and `sudo sshd -T | grep -iE 'pubkeyauth|allowusers|authorizedkeysfile'` for cause 2. **CORRECTED 2026-08-07 — the diagnosis above is WRONG. Nothing on melehost changed; the cause is entirely client-side.** Saiful pushed back with *"This is impossible. No one has used melehost other than me"*, which was the right challenge and the reason this was found. `~/.ssh/id_ed25519` is **passphrase-protected** — its header reads `aes256-ctr` + `bcrypt`, and `ssh-keygen -y -f` prompts for a passphrase rather than printing the public key. The `Host melehost` block carries `UseKeychain yes` + `AddKeysToAgent yes`, i.e. the passphrase normally comes from the macOS login Keychain. When the Keychain stopped supplying it (login keychain locked on sleep or screen-lock, or ssh-agent restarted — `ssh-add -l` reported *no identities* and `ssh-add --apple-load-keychain` loaded nothing), ssh could still OFFER the public key but could not sign the challenge with the private half, and every probe ran under `-o BatchMode=yes` — as did `publish_playstore.sh`'s scp — so it could not prompt and failed silently. **The server's reply to an unsigned challenge is byte-identical to its reply to an unauthorised key**, which is precisely why the earlier reasoning went wrong: `ssh -v` showing `Offering public key: … explicit` followed by `Permission denied (publickey,password)` is consistent with BOTH, and the 'clean protocol-level rejection ⇒ server-side' inference does not hold. Every supporting observation (host reachable, port open, host key unchanged, all three identities rejected alike) was true and equally consistent with the real cause — notably *all three keys failing* should have been the tell, since it is far more likely that one client cannot sign than that three separate keys were de-authorised at once. **Fix, client-side, one command:** `ssh-add --apple-use-keychain ~/.ssh/id_ed25519` — prompts once, loads the agent and re-stores the passphrase in the Keychain. Nothing to do on melehost: no `authorized_keys` edit, no `sshd_config` change, no fail2ban jail, no disk check. **Alpha was never affected** and the earlier verification of that stands. **The lesson, and it is the second instance of this class this week:** a symptom observed through a client that cannot prove itself says nothing about the server. The `ssh -v` line names the key being *offered*, not *accepted*, and I read the first as the second. The cheap check that would have settled it in one step — `ssh-keygen -y -f <key>`, which distinguishes an encrypted key from a usable one — cost nothing and was run only after being challenged. | fixed | [scripts/publish_playstore.sh](../../scripts/publish_playstore.sh) | AT:R66 |

But an analyst fact sheet that asserts its own liveness while potentially rendering a random walk is the same class as DEF052's fabricated technicals, arriving through a different door. **Fix:** make the mock arm unreachable when `use_real_market_data` is true, or thread a provenance flag out of the provider so `field_state["technicals"]` can record MOCK and the renderer can strip it — the second is honest, the first is safer for a live product. **(b) Loaded level label.** `breakout = max(highs[-_SMA_LONG:])` is simply the 50-day high, but it is rendered to the agent as `breakout level: $Y` in both the context block and `room_runner.py`'s scripted template. Naming resistance "the breakout level" tells the model the only valid long entry is *above the 50-day high*.
